stops.title: Rate of reaction, rate law & order/molecularity
stops.inShort: Average rate = −Δ[R]/Δt = +Δ[P]/Δt. Rate law: rate = k[A]^x[B]^y; overall order = x + y. Molecularity is the number of reacting species in an elementary step (always a positive integer).

stops.title: Integrated rate laws (Zero & First order) and half-life
stops.inShort: Zero order: [A]_t = [A]₀ − kt, t_½ = [A]₀/(2k), k unit: mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. First order: k = (2.303/t) log₁₀([A]₀/[A]_t), t_½ = 0.693/k (independent of [A]₀), k unit: s⁻¹.

stops.title: Collision theory & Arrhenius equation
stops.inShort: Arrhenius equation: k = A e^(−E_a / RT), log₁₀(k₂/k₁) = (E_a / 2.303 R) (T₂ − T₁)/(T₁ T₂). A reaction occurs when colliding molecules have energy ≥ E_a and proper orientation.

items.s: t_½ is independent of initial concentration.
Unit of k is mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.

board.text: The rate law equation for A → Product is rate = k[A]^x. What is the effect of increase in concentration of 'A' on rate of reaction, if x < 0?
board.answer: If x < 0, rate = k / [A]^|x|, so increasing concentration of 'A' decreases the rate of reaction.

points.text: Rate of reaction decreases when [A] increases (since x < 0)

board.text: Derive the relation between half life and rate constant for a first order reaction.
board.answer:
For a first order reaction: k = (2.303 / t) log₁₀([A]₀ / [A]_t).
At half-life t = t_½, [A]_t = [A]₀ / 2.
k = (2.303 / t_½) log₁₀(2) = (2.303 × 0.3010) / t_½ = 0.693 / t_½.
Therefore t_½ = 0.693 / k.

points.text: Integrated first order equation with [A]_t = [A]₀/2 at t = t_½

board.text: Define zero order reaction. A reaction takes place in two steps: (i) NO(g) + Cl₂(g) → NOCl₂(g) (ii) NOCl₂(g) + NO(g) → 2NOCl(g). Write the overall reaction and identify the reaction intermediate.
board.answer:
Zero order reaction: A reaction whose rate is independent of the concentration of reactants (rate = k[A]⁰ = k).
Overall reaction (adding steps i and ii): 2NO(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2NOCl(g).
Reaction intermediate: NOCl₂(g) (formed in step 1 and consumed in step 2).

board.text: If unit of rate constant is mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹, the order of reaction would be ____.
board.answer: (a) zero (for nth order, unit is mol^(1−n) dm^(3(n−1)) s⁻¹; for n = 0, mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹).

board.text: For the reaction A + B → P. If [B] is doubled at constant [A], the rate of reaction doubled. If [A] is tripled and [B] is doubled, the rate of reaction increases by a factor of 6. Calculate the rate law equation.
board.answer:
Let rate = k [A]^x [B]^y.
1. Doubling [B] at constant [A] doubles rate: 2^y = 2 ⇒ y = 1.
2. Tripling [A] and doubling [B] increases rate 6 times: 3^x · 2^1 = 6 ⇒ 3^x = 3 ⇒ x = 1.
Rate law equation: rate = k [A] [B] (overall order = 2).
